hunks.sol: Then his gaze settled squarely on me, and the people around us erupted as if a dam had burst.

hunks.sol: The Emperor was asking *me*, of all people, what should be done with the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord.

hunks.sol: “How could Your Majesty, the sovereign of all under Heaven, ask a mere subject—not even a minister of the court, but a lawless ruffian from the martial world—”

hunks.baseline: “Lawless ruffians from the martial world, you say.”
hunks.sol: “A lawless ruffian from the martial world.”

hunks.baseline: The Emperor muttered softly and looked around. Before I knew it, officials in full court dress had surrounded him on every side.
hunks.sol: The Emperor repeated the words quietly and looked around. Officials in court robes had gathered on every side of him.

hunks.baseline: The Emperor turned his gaze from one face to the next. The Emperor and the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had been so focused entirely on each other that many of these officials had survived. Then the Emperor continued, slowly.

hunks.baseline: “It is a strange thing. The martial-world ruffian you speak of fought desperately and ended up covered in blood, while you ministers of the court somehow look untouched after such a fierce battle.”
hunks.sol: “How strange,” the Emperor said at last. “The ruffian you speak of fought so hard he’s covered in blood. Yet you ministers of the court have come through this fierce battle looking remarkably untouched.”

hunks.baseline: Silence fell in an instant.
hunks.sol: Silence fell.

hunks.baseline: The Emperor’s words shut everyone up. He turned his head toward me.
hunks.sol: Having shut everyone up with a few words, the Emperor turned back to me.

hunks.baseline: I didn’t know.

hunks.sol: I didn’t know why he’d singled me out, or what answer he wanted.

hunks.baseline: Or what answer he wanted from me.
A single, explosive question that no one had expected. I heard people around us catch their breath.
hunks.sol: People caught their breath all around us.

hunks.baseline: Even the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord stopped laughing and opened his eyes wide.
hunks.sol: Even the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord stopped laughing and stared at me, eyes wide.

hunks.baseline: But the Emperor looked at me without wavering and answered.
hunks.sol: The Emperor’s gaze didn’t waver.

hunks.baseline: I wasn’t asking because I truly didn’t know the answer to this outrageous question.
hunks.sol: I wasn’t asking because I didn’t know.

hunks.baseline: Everyone needed to know.
hunks.sol: Everyone here needed to hear the answer, even if the people beyond the palace walls never did.

hunks.baseline: Even if no one outside the imperial palace ever learned the truth, the people here needed to hear it.
I believed the Emperor understood that much, too.
hunks.sol: I trusted the Emperor to understand what I was doing.

hunks.baseline: “He is a traitor without equal in all history. For many years, he blinded and deafened My Father, and used poison to slowly drive most of the imperial family—including My Crown Prince Brother—to their deaths.”
hunks.sol: “He is a traitor without equal in history. For years, he kept My Father blind and deaf to what was happening. He used poison to slowly drive most of the imperial family to their deaths, including My Eldest Brother, the Crown Prince.”

hunks.baseline: A ripple of shock spread through the crowd.
hunks.sol: Shock rippled through the crowd.

hunks.baseline: Everyone held their breath at the hidden history that had never been revealed.

hunks.baseline: As far as the world knew, the root of all evil was the Emperor himself.

hunks.sol: “By the time I learned the truth, it was too late. Traitors bent on destroying the Great Nation had seized control of the imperial family and held most of the real power.”

hunks.sol: An Emperor reduced to a puppet. Princes already poisoned.

hunks.sol: Those heirs to a noble bloodline had neither time nor people left to turn to.

hunks.sol: Except for an old general who had kept the Embroidered Uniform Guard loyal, and the Great Nation’s fourth prince, who had spent his days wandering the provinces, far from the throne.

hunks.sol: And so a restoration took place under the guise of a rebellion.

hunks.sol: Hundreds of court ministers died in a single night. Before long, tens of thousands more had been exiled or executed.

hunks.baseline: Even his small steps, with his growing years not yet behind him, carried him forward.
